content_metadata.description: Follow Lockpicking Dev as they pick and disassemble an ACE Series A527 padlock against the stunning backdrop of the Tetons.

qAndA.answer: Lockpicking Dev opened an ACE Series A527 padlock.
qAndA.question: What type of padlock did Lockpicking Dev open?

qAndA.answer: Lockpicking Dev opens the padlock in front of Colter Bay in Grand Teton National Park.
qAndA.question: What is the location where Lockpicking Dev opens the lock?

qAndA.answer: Lockpicking Dev points out a small disc in the padlock that is meant to prevent lock bumping.
qAndA.question: What security feature does the ACE padlock have to prevent lock bumping?

qAndA.answer: When Lockpicking Dev was picking the lock, they had to set the fifth pin twice for the lock to open. This indicated that the fifth pin was a spool.
qAndA.question: Why does Lockpicking Dev feel the fifth pin of the lock was a spool pin?

qAndA.answer: Yes, Lockpicking Dev recommends this padlock for lockpicking practice. They bought a different ACE padlock from their local Ace Hardware store.
qAndA.question: Does Lockpicking Dev recommend the ACE Series A527 padlock?
